motion-representations-s3.title: A ball tossed up from a balcony
motion-representations-s3.html:
A student on a balcony 15 m above the ground throws a ball straight up at 12 m/s. The ball rises, stops for an instant, then falls past the balcony to the ground. Air resistance is negligible. Take up as positive and g = 9.8 m/s².

Key: gold arrow, the initial velocity; dashed line, the path of the ball.

motion-representations-s4.html:
A car travels at 25 m/s on a straight road. The driver sees a stop sign, and 0.60 s later (the reaction time) starts braking. While braking, the car slows with a constant acceleration of −6.0 m/s² (forward is positive) until it stops.

Key: gold arrow, velocity; the gray stretch is covered during the reaction time, the red stretch while braking.

An airport walkway 48 m long moves to the right at 1.2 m/s relative to the floor. Ana walks to the right on it at 1.8 m/s relative to the walkway. Ben stands still on the walkway. Cara stands on the floor beside it. Right is positive.

Key: orange arrow, the walkway's velocity relative to the floor; gold arrow, Ana's velocity relative to the walkway. Arrow lengths are to scale.

items.q: What total distance does Mia walk?

mistakes.why: Value: 2 m is the size of her displacement (start to end). Distance counts every meter walked: 5 m out and 7 m back.
Value: 5 m is leg 1 alone. Distance adds every leg: 5 m out plus 7 m back.

items.q: What is Mia's displacement for the whole walk? Use a negative number for a displacement to the left.

mistakes.why: Value: 12 m is the distance, the length of her path. Displacement only compares where she ended (0 m) with where she started (+2 m).
Value: −7 m is only leg 2. Displacement for the whole walk compares the final position with the very first one.

items.q: How does the size of Mia's displacement compare with the distance she walks?
options: It is equal, because both describe the same walk
It is larger, because displacement includes a direction
It is smaller, because displacement is measured in a different unit
It is smaller, because she reversed direction partway

items.q: During leg 2, what is the sign of Mia's velocity?
options: Positive, because she is still at positive positions
Positive, because speed is a positive number
Negative, because she moves toward smaller x
Zero, because she ends up back near the start

items.q: After leg 2, Mia walks a third leg so that her displacement for the entire walk becomes zero. Where does she finish?
options: At the 0 m mark
At the +2 m mark
At the +7 m mark
At the −2 m mark

items.q: What total distance does the robot travel in the four legs?

mistakes.why: Value: 1.5 m is the displacement, where the signs cancel. Distance adds every leg as a positive length.

items.q: What is the robot's total displacement? Give a signed value (east is positive).

mistakes.why: Value: 40.5 m is the distance. A displacement adds the legs as vectors, so the westward legs are negative.
Value: 21 m adds only the eastward legs. The westward legs are negative and must be added too.

items.q: In which leg does the robot have the greatest speed?
options: Leg 1
Leg 2
Leg 4
Leg 3

items.q: What is the robot's velocity during leg 2? Give a signed value in m/s (east is positive).

mistakes.why: Value: you divided the time by the displacement. Velocity is displacement divided by time.

items.q: The robot makes a fifth leg that takes it back to exactly where it started. What is the displacement of that leg?
options: 0 m

items.q: Which of these quantities is a scalar?
options: The displacement of a runner
The velocity of a runner
The position of a runner on a track
The distance a runner covers

items.q: A bus drives 235 m north along a straight street, then 410 m south. Taking north as positive, what is its total displacement?

mistakes.why: Value: 645 m is the distance driven. For displacement, the southward leg is negative.
Value: the size is right, but the bus ends south of its start, so with north positive the displacement is −175 m.

items.q: Two cyclists ride along the same straight road at 6.0 m/s, one heading east and one heading west. Which statement is correct?
options: They have equal speeds and equal velocities
They have equal speeds but different velocities
They have different speeds but equal velocities
They have different speeds and different velocities

items.q: Which statement about a trip along a straight road is correct?
options: The size of the displacement is at most equal to the distance
The distance is at most equal to the size of the displacement
The distance and the size of the displacement are equal for a trip that ends where it started
The size of the displacement grows each time the traveler turns around

items.q: A ball sits at x = −3.0 m on a number line where east is positive. A student redraws the axis with the same origin but west as positive. What is the ball's position now?
options: 0 m

items.q: A runner's velocity is −4.2 m/s, with east positive. What is the runner's speed?

mistakes.why: Value: speed is the size of the velocity and is never negative. Drop the sign: 4.2 m/s.

items.q: The cart's velocity changes by the same amount in each 0.5 s interval. What is its acceleration at t = 1.5 s, the instant its velocity is zero?
options: Zero, because the cart is momentarily at rest
The same as at the other readings: negative, not zero
Positive, because the cart is about to turn around
It is undefined, because Δt is zero at a single instant

items.q: What is the cart's average acceleration from t = 0 to t = 1.0 s? Give a signed value and its unit.

mistakes.why: Value: the size is right, but Δv is final minus initial, 0.40 − 1.20, which is negative.

items.q: From t = 1.5 s to t = 2.5 s, the cart rolls back down the ramp. During this time its acceleration is negative. What is happening to its speed?
options: It decreases, because a negative acceleration means slowing down
It stays the same, because the acceleration does not change
It decreases, because the velocity values are below zero
It increases, because the velocity and acceleration have the same sign

items.q: What is the cart's change in velocity, Δv, from t = 0 to t = 2.5 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 0.40 m/s treats the two speeds as if they were in the same direction. Subtract with signs: −0.80 − (+1.20) = −2.00 m/s.
Value: you dropped the minus sign of the final velocity. The cart is moving down the ramp at 2.5 s, so v(final) = −0.80 m/s.

items.q: The ramp keeps going and the pattern continues. What velocity will the detector read at t = 3.5 s?
Which car has a negative acceleration and is speeding up?
options: Car 3
Car 2
Car 4
Car 1

items.q: Car 2 has a velocity of +12 m/s and an acceleration of −3.0 m/s². What is its velocity 2.0 s later?

mistakes.why: Value: 18 m/s adds the change, but the acceleration points opposite to the velocity, so Δv is −6.0 m/s.
Value: −6.0 m/s is Δv, the change. Add it to the starting velocity of +12 m/s.

items.q: Car 4 has a velocity of −8.0 m/s and an acceleration of +2.0 m/s². What is its speed 1.5 s later?

mistakes.why: Value: 11 m/s adds 3.0 to the speed. The acceleration points opposite to the velocity, so the car slows: 8.0 − 3.0 = 5.0 m/s.
Value: −5.0 m/s is the velocity. The speed is its size, with no sign.

items.q: Car 1 and car 3 have accelerations of the same size. What is true of both cars over the next second?
options: Car 1 speeds up and car 3 slows down
Both speed up by the same amount
Both slow down, because their accelerations point in opposite directions
Neither changes speed, because their accelerations cancel

items.q: What is the ball's average velocity from 2.0 s to 3.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 1.2 m/s divides the final position by the final time. Use the changes: Δx ÷ Δt.

items.q: What is the ball's average velocity from 2.0 s to 2.1 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 0.84 m/s divides a position by a clock reading. Average velocity uses the change in position over the change in time.
Value: 0.164 m is the displacement; divide it by the 0.1 s interval.

items.q: The average velocities from 2.0 s to 3.0 s, to 2.5 s and to 2.1 s are 2.0, 1.8 and 1.64 m/s. What is the best estimate of the ball's instantaneous velocity at exactly 2.0 s?
options: 2.0 m/s, because the longest interval uses the most data
About 1.8 m/s, the middle of the three values
About 1.6 m/s, the value the shrinking intervals approach
0.80 m/s, the position at 2.0 s divided by the time

items.q: What does the data show about the ball's motion between 2.0 s and 3.0 s?
options: It moves at a steady velocity, since the position increases each time
It is speeding up, since later equal intervals cover more distance
It is slowing down, since the average velocity gets smaller for shorter intervals
It is at rest at 2.0 s, since the ball started from rest

items.q: A sprinter starts from rest and reaches 9.0 m/s in 1.8 s. What is her average acceleration?

mistakes.why: Value: you multiplied. Acceleration is the change in velocity divided by the time interval.
Value: the fraction is upside down. Acceleration is Δv ÷ Δt, in (m/s)/s = m/s².

items.q: A delivery van drives 12.0 km east in 10.0 min, then 4.0 km west in 5.0 min. What is the size of its average velocity for the whole trip, in m/s?

mistakes.why: Value: about 18 m/s is the average speed, total distance over time. Average velocity uses the displacement, 8.0 km east.
Value: you divided by 15 minutes without converting. 15.0 min = 900 s.
Value: about 17 m/s averages the two legs' speeds (20 and 13 m/s). That drops the direction of the second leg and ignores that the legs last different times. Use total displacement ÷ total time.
Value: 3.3 m/s averages the two legs' velocities (+20 and −13 m/s), but the legs last different times. Use total displacement ÷ total time.

items.q: Two bikes each gain 6.0 m/s of velocity. Bike A takes 3.0 s and bike B takes 1.5 s. How does bike B's average acceleration compare with bike A's?
options: Half as large
The same, because both gain 6.0 m/s
Twice as large
Four times as large

items.q: A 4.5 m long car drives 2.0 km along a straight highway. Why may the car be treated as a single point when finding its average velocity?
options: In physics problems, every car is treated as having no size at all
Its length is tiny next to 2.0 km, and all its parts move together
Its mass is small compared with the mass of the road it drives on
A point model gives the car a larger average velocity than it has

items.q: A runner moves around a circular track at a steady 5.0 m/s. Is the runner accelerating?
options: Yes, because the direction of the velocity keeps changing
No, because the speed does not change
No, because the runner ends each lap where it began
Yes, because 5.0 m/s is a large speed

items.q: What is the car's acceleration from t = 0 to t = 4.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 24 is the area under the graph, which is the displacement in meters. Acceleration is the slope.
Value: the slope is rise over run, Δv ÷ Δt, not Δt ÷ Δv.

items.q: How far does the car travel from t = 0 to t = 14 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 168 m treats the car as moving at 12 m/s the whole time. The triangles at the start and end are only half as large as rectangles.
Value: 72 m is only the cruising part. Add the areas of the triangles for speeding up and slowing down.

items.q: During which interval is the car's acceleration negative?
options: From 0 to 4 s
From 4 s to 10 s
At no time, since the velocity stays positive
From 10 s to 14 s

items.q: Which describes the car's position-time graph from 10 s to 14 s?
options: Falling in a straight line from 10 s to 14 s
Rising and getting steeper until 14 s
Rising, less and less steeply, level at 14 s
A horizontal line from 10 s to 14 s

items.q: What is the car's average velocity for the whole 14 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 6.0 m/s averages the start and peak velocities, which only works for a single constant acceleration. Use total displacement ÷ total time.
Value: 12 m/s is the cruising speed. The car was slower than that while speeding up and slowing down.

items.q: What is runner B's velocity?

mistakes.why: Value: 3.75 m/s divides B's final position by the time. B started at 10 m, so use the change in position: 30 − 10 = 20 m.

items.q: At t = 4.0 s, the two lines cross. What is true at that instant?
options: The runners have the same velocity
The runners are at the same position and have the same velocity
Runner B is just catching up to runner A
The runners are at the same position, but A is faster

items.q: Which runner has the greater acceleration?
options: Runner A, because A's line is steeper
Runner B, because B started farther along
Neither; both accelerations are zero
Runner A, because A covers more distance

items.q: How far apart are the runners at t = 6.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 30 m is A's position. Subtract B's position, 25 m.

items.q: Which describes the two runners' velocity-time graphs?
options: Two horizontal lines, A's higher than B's
Two lines crossing at t = 4.0 s
Two rising lines, A's steeper
A horizontal line for A and a rising line for B

items.q: How long does the ball take to reach its highest point? Use g = 9.8 m/s².

mistakes.why: Value: 2.4 s is the time to rise and fall back to the balcony. The top is halfway, where v = 0.
Value: 1.6 s is √(2v₀/g), as if 12 m/s were a distance in Δy = ½gt². At the top v = 0, so use v = v₀ + at.

items.q: How high above the balcony does the ball rise? Use g = 9.8 m/s².

mistakes.why: Value: 15 m forgets the 2 in v² = v₀² + 2aΔy. Δy = v₀²/(2g).
Value: the initial velocity must be squared: Δy = v₀²/(2g) = 144/19.6.

items.q: What is the ball's acceleration at its highest point?
options: Zero, because the ball is momentarily at rest
9.8 m/s² downward
9.8 m/s² upward, because the ball was thrown up
Smaller than 9.8 m/s², because the ball has slowed down

items.q: As the ball falls back past the balcony, what is its velocity?
options: 12 m/s downward
12 m/s upward
Zero
24 m/s downward

items.q: At what speed does the ball hit the ground, 15 m below the balcony? Use g = 9.8 m/s².

mistakes.why: Value: 17 m/s treats the ball as dropped from rest. It was thrown at 12 m/s, so v₀² = 144 m²/s² must be included.
Value: speeds do not add like that. Use v² = v₀² + 2aΔy, which adds the squares.
Value: 438 is v², in m²/s². Take the square root.

items.q: How far does the car travel during the 0.60 s reaction time?

mistakes.why: Value: 7.5 m treats the car as slowing during the reaction time. It is not braking yet, so the velocity stays 25 m/s.

items.q: How far does the car travel while braking?

mistakes.why: Value: 104 m forgets the 2 in v² = v₀² + 2aΔx. Δx = v₀²/(2|a|).
Value: the initial velocity must be squared: (25 m/s)² = 625 m²/s².

items.q: How long does the braking last?

mistakes.why: Value: 4.8 s includes the reaction time. The question asks only about the braking.

items.q: The same car approaches at 1.5 times the speed with the same braking acceleration. How does its braking distance change?
options: It becomes 1.5 times as long
It becomes 3 times as long
It stays the same, because the braking is the same
It becomes 2.25 times as long

items.q: Which velocity-time graph matches the car from the moment the driver sees the sign until it stops?
options: A straight line down from 25 m/s to zero, starting at t = 0
Flat at 25 m/s for 0.60 s, then a curve that gets steeper
Flat at 25 m/s for 0.60 s, then a straight line down to zero
Flat at 25 m/s for 0.60 s, then a drop straight down to zero

items.q: A cart starts with a known velocity and speeds up with a known constant acceleration over a measured distance. The time is not known and not asked for. Which equation gives its final velocity most directly?
options: v = v₀ + at
v² = v₀² + 2a(x − x₀)
x = x₀ + v₀t + ½at²
v(avg) = Δx/Δt

items.q: A stone dropped from rest takes 0.60 s to fall to the bottom of a dry well. How long would it take to fall from a height 4 times as great? Air resistance is negligible.

mistakes.why: Value: 2.4 s treats time as proportional to height. Height grows as t², so time grows as the square root of height.
Value: time grows as the square root of the height, not as its square.

items.q: A sprinter leaves the blocks and her velocity-time graph curves: it rises steeply at first, then less and less steeply until it is flat. What does this show?
options: Her acceleration is constant until she reaches top speed
She slows down after the start
Her acceleration increases as she gets faster
Her acceleration is largest at the start and decreases to zero

items.q: An acceleration-time graph for a cart is a horizontal line at +0.40 m/s² from t = 0 to t = 5.0 s. The cart's velocity at t = 0 is +0.30 m/s. What is its velocity at t = 5.0 s?

mistakes.why: Value: 2.0 m/s is the change in velocity (the area). Add the starting velocity, 0.30 m/s.
Value: under a horizontal line the area is a rectangle, height × width, with no ½.

items.q: A motion diagram shows a cart's positions at equal time intervals. The dots get closer together from left to right while the cart moves right. What are the directions of its velocity and acceleration?
options: Velocity to the right, acceleration to the right
Velocity to the right, acceleration to the left
Velocity to the left, acceleration to the left
Velocity to the right, zero acceleration

items.q: A ball is dropped from rest off a bridge. Air resistance is negligible. Predict how each quantity changes from 1.0 s after release to 2.0 s after release.

variables.name: The distance it falls in each 0.10 s

items.q: What is Ana's velocity relative to the floor, as Cara measures it?

mistakes.why: Value: 0.60 m/s subtracts the walkway's velocity. Both point right, so they add.

items.q: How long does Ana take to cover the 48 m walkway?

mistakes.why: Value: 27 s uses only her walking speed. The walkway carries her too, so use 3.0 m/s relative to the floor.

items.q: What is Ana's velocity as Ben measures it?
options: Zero, because they are both on the walkway

items.q: What is Cara's velocity as Ben measures it?
options: Zero, because Cara is standing still

items.q: Ana turns around and walks to the left at 1.8 m/s relative to the walkway. What is her velocity relative to the floor?

mistakes.why: Value: −3.0 m/s gives the walkway the wrong sign. It still moves right, +1.2 m/s.
Value: the size is right, but she walks left faster than the walkway carries her right, so her velocity is negative.

items.q: What is the car's velocity relative to the truck?

mistakes.why: Value: 51 m/s adds the velocities. To change frames from the road to the truck, subtract the truck's velocity.
Value: −7.0 m/s is the truck's velocity relative to the car. The car is the faster one, so relative to the truck it moves forward.

items.q: What is the motorcycle's velocity relative to the truck?

mistakes.why: Value: 5.0 m/s adds the truck's velocity. Subtract it: −17 − (+22) = −39 m/s.
Value: the size is right, but the motorcycle moves west relative to the truck, so its velocity is negative.

items.q: Which observer sees the motorcycle moving with the greatest speed?
options: The truck's driver
A person standing at the roadside
The car's driver
Each of the three measures an equal speed

items.q: The truck's driver brakes, and her velocity relative to the road drops steadily from +22 m/s to +16 m/s in 3.0 s. The car keeps a steady +29 m/s. What is the car's acceleration as measured from the truck?
options: Zero, because the car moves at a steady velocity
+2.0 m/s², because the truck slows while the car does not
−2.0 m/s², the same as the truck's acceleration
+29 m/s², because the car's velocity is 29 m/s

items.q: What is the boat's velocity relative to the bank on the downstream trip?

mistakes.why: Value: going downstream, the current points the same way as the boat, so the velocities add.

items.q: How long does the upstream return trip take?

mistakes.why: Value: 55 s is the downstream time. Upstream the current works against the boat: 4.0 − 1.5 = 2.5 m/s.
Value: 75 s ignores the current. Relative to the bank the boat moves at 2.5 m/s upstream.

items.q: How does the round-trip time on the river compare with the time for the same 600 m round trip on still water?
options: It is the same, because the current helps one way and hurts the other
It is shorter on the river
It is longer on the river
A comparison needs the mass of the boat

items.q: A passenger on the boat walks toward the stern (the back) at 1.0 m/s relative to the boat during the downstream trip. What is her velocity relative to the bank?

A cart on a flatcar speeds up from rest to 0.60 m/s relative to the flatcar in 2.0 s. The flatcar moves at a constant 5.0 m/s relative to the ground. What is the cart's acceleration relative to the ground?
options: 0.30 m/s², the same as relative to the flatcar
2.8 m/s², because the flatcar's velocity adds 5.0 m/s
Zero, because the cart rides on the flatcar
2.5 m/s², the flatcar's velocity divided by 2.0 s

items.q: You sit in a train at rest in a station and see the train beside yours start to move forward. A moment later you realize it is your own train moving backward. Why could you not tell at first?
options: Your train was moving too slowly to have a velocity
The other train had a larger velocity than yours
Motion is visible to a person on the ground, not to a passenger
You saw relative motion, and either train moving looks the same

items.q: A cyclist rides east at 8.0 m/s relative to the road into a wind blowing west at 5.0 m/s relative to the road. What wind speed does the cyclist feel, relative to herself?

mistakes.why: Value: 3.0 m/s would be the wind she feels if the wind blew east, with her. A headwind and her own motion add.

items.q: How long is the ball in the air?

mistakes.why: Value: 0.33 s divides the height by the horizontal speed. The fall time comes from the vertical motion alone: Δy = ½gt².
Value: you forgot the square root: t² = 2Δy/g, so t = √(2Δy/g).

items.q: How far from the base of the table does the ball land (the distance d)?

mistakes.why: Value: there is no ½ in the horizontal motion. With no horizontal acceleration, d = vₓt.
Value: 0.80 m is the height of the table, not the horizontal distance. Find the fall time from the height (0.40 s), then d = vₓt.

items.q: The ball leaves the same table at 4.8 m/s instead. How does its time in the air compare?
options: It is twice as long
It is half as long
It is √2 times as long
It is the same, 0.40 s

items.q: What is the ball's speed just before it hits the floor?

mistakes.why: Value: 6.4 m/s adds the components as numbers. They are perpendicular, so combine them with the Pythagorean theorem.
Value: 4.0 m/s is only the vertical component. The ball still moves sideways at 2.4 m/s.

items.q: Which statement about the ball's velocity while it is in the air is correct?
options: Its horizontal component slows down as the ball falls
Its horizontal part is steady; its vertical part grows
Both components grow at the same rate
Its vertical component stays zero until it lands

items.q: Using the table, what is the ball's horizontal velocity?

mistakes.why: Value: 18.0 m/s is the launch speed along the 37° direction. Only its horizontal component, v cos θ, shows up in x.
Value: 10.8 m/s is the vertical component, v sin θ.

items.q: At what time does the ball reach its highest point?

mistakes.why: Value: 2.21 s is the whole flight. The top comes halfway, when v<sub>y</sub> = 0.
Value: use the vertical component, 18.0 sin 37.0° = 10.8 m/s, not the full launch speed.

items.q: Which describes a graph of the ball's vertical velocity v<sub>y</sub> against time (up positive)?
options: A horizontal line at 14.4 m/s
A curve that rises and then falls, like the path of the ball
A straight line sloping down, crossing zero near 1.1 s
A straight line sloping down that stops at zero

items.q: Where does the ball land, measured horizontally from the kick?

mistakes.why: Value: 15.9 m is where the ball is at its highest point. On level ground the flight takes twice as long.
Value: use the horizontal component of the velocity, 14.4 m/s, not 18.0 m/s.

items.q: The ball is kicked again at 18.0 m/s but at 53.0° (so sin and cos swap). How do the new range and time of flight compare with the 37.0° kick?
options: The same range, but a longer time of flight
A longer range and a longer time of flight
A shorter range and the same time of flight
The same range and the same time of flight

items.q: How long does the package take to reach the ground?

mistakes.why: Value: take the square root: t² = 2Δy/g = 4.08 s², so t = 2.0 s.
Value: the fall time comes from the vertical motion alone, not from 20 m ÷ 6.0 m/s.

items.q: How far ahead of the target should the drone release the package, measured horizontally?

mistakes.why: Value: released straight above the target, the package would land 12 m past it: it keeps moving forward at 6.0 m/s.
Value: there is no ½ in the horizontal motion, since aₓ = 0.

items.q: Where is the package relative to the drone while it falls, if the drone keeps flying at 6.0 m/s?
options: Behind the drone, falling farther back each second
Directly below the drone the whole time
Ahead of the drone, pulling farther in front of it
At the drone's height, moving sideways

items.q: Which describes the package's path as seen by a person standing on the ground?
options: A downward curve that gets steeper
A straight line down
A straight slanted line toward the target
A curve that rises first, then falls

items.q: At the highest point of a ball's flight after being thrown at an angle, which is true? Air resistance is negligible.
options: Its velocity and acceleration are both zero
Its velocity is zero and its acceleration is g downward
Its velocity is horizontal and its acceleration is zero
Its velocity is horizontal; its acceleration is g down

items.q: Two balls roll off the edges of two tables at the same horizontal speed. Table B is 4.0 times as high as table A. Ball A lands 0.50 m from its table. How far from its table does ball B land?

mistakes.why: Value: 2.0 m assumes d ∝ h. The fall time grows as √h, so d grows by √4 = 2.
Value: d grows as √h, not h².

items.q: A ball is launched at 25 m/s, 60.° above the horizontal. What is the vertical component of its initial velocity? (Degree mode.)

mistakes.why: Value: 13 m/s is the horizontal component. The vertical side is opposite the angle from the ground: use sine.
